An explosion at the Fabrica de Municiones de Granada (FMG), an ammunition factory on the outskirts of Granada, Spain, injured three people on the morning of Oct. 30, Spanish newspaper ABC reported.

Emergency services received multiple calls reporting the blast, which was felt in nearby towns, including Fuente Vaqueros and La Zubia, Spanish outlet El Espanol reported.
All three people sustained minor injuries, including hearing damage, ABC reported.

Russia’s Justice Ministry has added the Dialogue with Russian Democratic Forces at the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) to its list of “undesirable” organizations, a move that renders affiliation with the anti-war group illegal.
The delegation of Russian exiles was set up in January after years of lobbying efforts by leading opposition figures like former businessman Mikhail Khodorkovsky.
Several members of the anti-war group, including dissident Vladimir Kara-Murza and Pussy Riot co-founder Nadya Tolokonnikova, already face criminal prosecution in Russia.
Under Russian law, individuals affiliated with an “undesirable” entity can face up to four years in prison. Organizing the work of an “undesirable” group carries a maximum sentence of six years in prison.

shrnuti: Police detained a 55-year-old Russian man in the city of Świdnica, in Poland’s Lower Silesian Voivodeship, after he photographed trains and railway infrastructure, the newspaper Rzeczpospolita reported.

Russian man arrested in Poland on espionage charges after photographing trains
October 30, 2026, 2:42 pm
Source: Rzeczpospolita
Police detained a 55-year-old Russian man in the city of Świdnica, in Poland’s Lower Silesian Voivodeship, after he photographed trains and railway infrastructure, the newspaper Rzeczpospolita reported.
The detention came during a police operation to secure a soccer match. After the game ended, officers patrolling the city noticed a parked car near a railroad crossing. The man inside tried to flee when he spotted the police.
After stopping him, police found professional photography equipment and files showing he had photographed trains and critical railway and transportation infrastructure, not only in Poland.
He has been charged with espionage, and a court ordered him held in custody for three months. Under Polish law, the offense carries a minimum sentence of five years in prison. His name has not been released.

Advertisement
A Russian citizen was charged with espionage in Poland after he was caught taking photographs of the country’s railway infrastructure, police in Lower Silesia said Friday.
Authorities said officers patrolling after a football match in Świdnica, south-western Poland, stumbled upon the 55-year-old Russian national as he was taking photographs of passing trains at an unguarded railway crossing.
“Everything indicates that the photos he took could be used against the security of the state,” the regional police authority wrote in a press release .
Advertisement
Police found a large amount of evidence suggesting that the man took pictures of strategic infrastructure systematically. “There were photographs of various places and important communication facilities, not only in Poland,” Łukasz Dutkowiak, a spokesperson for the Lower Silesian police, told Radio Wrocław .
Prosecutors are now investigating “activities for foreign intelligence against the Republic of Poland,” the regional authority added.

Pentagon urges Baltic NATO allies to tone down rhetoric about Russia, citing remarks likening Putin to a ‘rat in a corner’
October 30, 2026, 8:49 am
Source: Reuters
Pentagon officials urged several NATO member countries to tone down their rhetoric about the Russian threat during bilateral meetings, according to Reuters sources.
The requests went to Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia, among others, the agency’s sources said. It is unclear whether other countries received similar requests.
Elbridge Colby, head of the Pentagon’s policy directorate, was one of the officials who conveyed the requests. He cited public statements by Europeans describing Russia as “cornered like a rat” as an example of inappropriate rhetoric.
It is unclear which statement he meant, but in late September, Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal called Putin a “rat in a corner” and suggested that Russia is resorting to sabotage in Europe because it is increasingly bogged down in the war with Ukraine, Reuters said.

shrnuti: At least 14 others were wounded in the attack in the central city of Dnipro, including an 11-year-old boy.

Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say - BBC News
Image source, State Emergency Service Of Ukraine
By Tom McArthur
Published
29 October 2026, 12:38 GMT
Updated 1 hour ago
At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said.
Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.
Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.
Russia's military has not publicly commented. It has repeatedly hit Ukraine's large railway network, but Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians.
In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to Ukrzaliznytsia head Oleksandr Pertsovsky. He said many people were on the platform when the Russian drone struck.
"But unfortunately there were still a large number of people on the platform," he said.

The deployment of 500 paratroopers to Milan to quell violent protests by teenagers marks a surprising shift in the use of soldiers to maintain public order. The sight of Lince tactical vehicles beneath the Gothic spires of Milan’s Duomo looked more like a government PR stunt than a solution to the unrest that had erupted in the city centre. And a look back at history seems to bear this out: in the past, bringing in the army has always marked dramatic moments in the country’s history.

FOD Financiën said it would extend some upcoming tax filing deadlines affected by the disruption, with new dates to be announced.

Schutz von Kritischer Infrastruktur
Bund beschließt mehr Prüfungen auf Sabotagerisiko
Stand: 28.10.2026 • 15:48 Uhr
Die Bedrohung für die Kritische Infrastruktur in Deutschland - etwa durch Sabotage oder Spionage - ist gestiegen. Daher will der Bund künftig Beschäftigte in noch mehr Betrieben auf mögliche Sicherheitsrisiken überprüfen.
Das Bundeskabinett hat eine Ausweitung der Sicherheitsüberprüfung von Beschäftigten in wichtigen Betrieben der Kritischen Infrastruktur beschlossen. Das soll das Risiko von Sabotageaktionen mit extremistischem Hintergrund oder im Auftrag eines ausländischen Geheimdienstes reduzieren.
Die Verordnung soll Einrichtungen wie etwa die Bahn oder Wasserwerke vor gefährlichen Eingriffen sogenannter Innentäter, also Menschen mit Zugang zu wichtigen Anlagen, schützen. Dafür wird neu bestimmt, welche Behörden und Unternehmensteile sicherheitsempfindlich sind.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre have opened a direct line to Vladimir Putin, drawing criticism from some fellow European leaders — even as Ukraine backs their efforts. Nicholas Vinocur and Paul Dallison examine the fallout and the growing scramble over who gets to speak for Europe in peace talks.

Norway and Finland hold rare call with Putin to discuss ending war - BBC News
Image source, AFP via Getty Images
Image caption, Norway and Finland say they are not acting on behalf of other European leaders
By Laura Gozzi   and   Hafsa Khalil
Published
27 October 2026, 13:12 GMT
Updated 1 hour ago
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said.
Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.
Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity…

The Slovo Zashchite project reported that Kynev was beaten so severely during his arrest that his leg was broken. Political scientist Ekaterina Schulmann said the beating was an attempt to force Kynev to confess to treason.

titulek: Leaders of Finland and Norway talk to Putin

vyrez.text:
Leaders of Finland and Norway talk to Putin – POLITICO
Skip to main content
Advertisement
Finland’s President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a joint call with Russian leader Vladimir Putin on Tuesday as part of international efforts to secure an end to the war in Ukraine.
“The discussion was frank and substantive,” said Stubb said in a statement after the call. “We are neighboring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions.”
The two leaders — who are firm allies of Ukraine — were not speaking as official representatives of Europe as a whole. The call was held in consultation with Ukraine.
Støre said the European leaders stressed the importance of de-escalation in the call with Putin. “The war comes with enormous human and material costs. The suffering and destruction will impact generations,” he added.
Their conversation comes at a highly sensitive moment as U.S. President Donald Trump pushes for a peace deal. Talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine are planned to take place in Abu Dhabi next month.

Melting glaciers in Dolomites reveal cache of first world war munitions
Italian army removes and defuses 250 explosives encased in ice for more than 100 years after hikers’ sightings
A significant cache of unexploded bombs from the first world war emerged this summer from rapidly retreating glaciers in the Dolomites, the Italian army has said.
The devices, which included Italian artillery shells and French mortar bombs, were removed and defused by the army’s Julia Alpine brigade, according to a statement.
The weapons originated from the white war, a battle between the Austro-Hungarian army and Italian troops across treacherous and bitterly cold terrain between 1915 and 1918.

Russian TV production designer dies in Moscow hospital after arrest on treason charges
October 26, 2026, 1:13 pm
Source: Department One
Alexander Kondratov, the production designer for the Russian TV series Likvidatsiya (Liquidation”), has died at Botkin Hospital in Moscow after being arrested on treason charges, the Russian human rights group Department One said.
Kondratov, 52, was taken to the hospital from a pretrial detention center on October 23, human rights activists said. Department One did not specify the cause of death or the source of that information.
Kondratov was born and raised in Moscow but had lived in Kyiv since 2012. He had traveled to Russia to renew his foreign passport and was detained at Vnukovo Airport. After a series of so-called “carousel arrests,” authorities opened a criminal case against him on treason charges. The case was based on “at least six publications” posted online. Their contents remain unknown.

Moscow mother of eight charged with financing terrorism over payment to ISIS
October 26, 2026, 8:33 am
Source: Meduza
Maria Davydova, a 31-year-old Moscow mother of eight, has been arrested on charges of financing terrorism.
The case was opened in July under Russia’s criminal statute against financing terrorism, and a court authorized her arrest. Davydova was added to Russia’s list of terrorists and extremists.
Citing a source in law enforcement, the Russian state news agency RIA Novosti reported in July that investigators believe Davydova transferred about 15,000 rubles to the Islamic State.
Case materials cited by the Russian state news agency TASS on October 26 state that Davydova “is self-employed, has eight dependent children, including young children and minors, is not married, and has a specialized secondary education.”
Russia’s criminal statute under which Davydova is charged allows for a sentence of up to life in prison.
A military court will hear Davydova’s case. The trial’s start date has not been announced.

titulek: Vrtěti psem: Proč Babiš spustil útok na Českou televizi
titulekPuvodni: Vrtěti psem: Proč Babiš spustil útok na Českou televizi
shrnuti: Vláda krátce po porážce v podzimních volbách rozjela své tažení za změnu financování České televize a Českého rozhlasu. Vezmeme vás na noční sněmovní jednání i na demonstrace do přilehlých ulic.

vyrez.text:
Vrtěti psem: Proč Babiš spustil útok na Českou televizi — Deník N
Premiér Andrej Babiš ve Sněmovně. Foto: Jakub Plíhal, Deník N
Vláda krátce po porážce v podzimních volbách rozjela své tažení za změnu financování České televize a Českého rozhlasu. Vezmeme vás na noční sněmovní jednání i na demonstrace do přilehlých ulic.
Více o poslechu Deníku N
Přidat Deník N mezi oblíbené zdroje
Čas 4.36 v sobotu ráno rozhodně není momentem, kdy by poslanci řešili zákony. Vládní koalice si pro svůj výpad proti veřejnoprávním médiím ale vybrala právě tento okamžik.
Změnu financování ČT a rozhlasu začaly špičky Babišovy koalice řešit silově a také překvapivě – a to až tak, že o tom předem neřekly ani vlastním poslancům.
Noční jednání tak provázely hádky, porušování zvyklostí i ohýbání jednacího řádu. A také protesty veřejnosti. Během celého jednání probíhala demonstrace v okolí Sněmovny, protesty pokračují také během víkendu.
V nové epizodě podcastu Vrtěti psem situaci probíráme s reportérkami Zdislavou Pokornou a Karolínou Blažkovou, které sledovaly jednání přímo na místě – v budově Sněmovny i v místě protestů.
Rozebíráme také, proč Babiš vůbec celou akci spustil.
Všechny díly podcastu…

LÆS OP
ORDBOG TEKST
Af
Jonas Foldager
Aleksander Boelt Bruun
I dag kl. 07:00
Over 40.000 mennesker søgte ned i Kyivs metro under Ruslands massive angreb i sommer. 
For over et år siden begyndte Metroselskabet at undersøge, om Københavns metro også kunne bruges som beskyttelsesrum, sådan som det sker i Kyiv.
Dengang lød det, at undersøgelsen ville være færdig inden for få måneder, men resultaterne fra arbejdet har endnu ikke set dagens lys.
Nu afslører hidtil fortrolige mails mellem Københavns Kommune og Metroselskabet, som DR har fået aktindsigt i, at metroen i dag ikke kan bruges som beskyttelsesrum.
I hvert fald ikke uden omfattende ændringer.
Det bekræfter Lene Sandberg, lektor ved Københavns Professionshøjskole. Hun forsker i samfundssikkerhed,…

Kyiv's power ring under attack: why the capital faces a winter of blackouts | Ukrainska Pravda
Hopes for a mild winter or inaccuracies in Russian strikes will not help Kyiv get through this winter without problems with its electricity supply. The only question is how long the power cuts will last and whether air defence forces and power engineers will manage to prevent the worst-case scenario.
The Russians are continuing their systematic attacks on Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast, seeking to completely destroy the city's combined heat and power plants and break the so-called power ring in order to plunge the capital entirely into darkness and cold.
The city has already lost a significant proportion of its own power generation capacity, while strikes are destroying substations through which electricity is supplied from other regions. In the event of severe frosts and further hits, a scenario involving 20 hours without electricity no longer seems far-fetched.
